purpose: Questions for source review. A matched facet does not answer a question.

checklists.scope: Historical holding: County of Maui, Supreme Court, No. 18-260, April 23, 2020. CWA discharge through groundwater.
checklists.limitations: The Court vacated and remanded. It did not decide whether a new project needs a permit. Check current law, receiving-water jurisdiction, permit coverage and site evidence separately.

sources.title: County of Maui v. Hawaii Wildlife Fund, opinion of the Court

questions.question: Does a pollutant leave an identified point source and reach jurisdictional surface water?
questions.evidence_needed: Outfall or injection plans, pollutant evidence and receiving-water determination.

questions.question: Does the groundwater route satisfy the functional-equivalent test?
questions.evidence_needed: Transit time, distance, intervening material, dilution or chemical change, relative quantity reaching water, manner or area of entry, and retained identity. Time and distance usually matter most.

checklists.scope: Historical holding: Sackett, Supreme Court, No. 21-454, May 25, 2023. Federal jurisdiction over adjacent wetlands.
checklists.limitations: This checklist covers the adjacent-wetlands holding, not every Section 404 condition or state wetland law. Seasonal interruptions, unlawful barriers, current regulations, exemptions and permit coverage need separate review.

sources.title: Sackett v. EPA, opinion of the Court

questions.question: Is the adjacent water a relatively permanent body connected to traditional interstate navigable waters?
Does the wetland have a continuous surface connection that makes it indistinguishable from that water?
questions.evidence_needed: Wetland delineation and connection evidence, including seasonal conditions and barriers.

checklists.scope: EPA construction-stormwater screening guidance, checked November 2, 2026.
checklists.limitations: Confirm the permitting authority, applicable permit version, discharge jurisdiction and any waiver. The proposed 2027 EPA CGP is a proposal; delegated state permits must be checked separately.

sources.title: EPA: Stormwater Discharges from Construction Activities
sources.locator: Background on Permitting Protections: What Construction Activities Are Regulated

questions.question: Will construction activity produce a regulated stormwater discharge?
questions.evidence_needed: Drainage plan, discharge routes and jurisdictional review.

questions.question: Will disturbance reach at least one acre, including a larger common plan of development or sale?
questions.evidence_needed: Disturbed acreage and the full common-development-plan boundary; a smaller individual parcel can still qualify.
